beats.subline: Tuesday, September 15, 2026 close — stocks fell for a second straight session as Treasury yields hit their highest level since 2007 ahead of the Fed's decision.
beats.body: Chip and AI-linked names extended their slide as the 10-year Treasury yield climbed to its highest level since 2007 and oil stayed elevated on Middle East supply worries, with investors bracing for the Fed's Wednesday rate decision.

beats.headline: Saudi crown prince meets CENTCOM chief in Jeddah as Houthis push toward Bab el-Mandeb Strait
beats.body: Mohammed bin Salman met Adm. Brad Cooper on Monday after separately pressing President Trump by phone for direct US strikes on Yemen's Houthis; Trump declined to authorize strikes but agreed to expand intelligence-sharing and targeting support for Saudi forces as the Iran-aligned group advances along the Red Sea coast toward the strategic Bab el-Mandeb chokepoint.

beats.headline: Taiwan tracks 15 PLA aircraft sorties and 8 PLA Navy ships in latest 24-hour count
beats.body: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense detected 15 PLA aircraft sorties, eight PLA Navy vessels and two official ships operating around the island in the 24 hours to 6 a.m. Wednesday, with 12 of the sorties crossing into Taiwan's northern, southwestern and eastern air defense zones as Beijing keeps up pressure ahead of Xi Jinping's September 24 Washington summit.

beats.headline: Pentagon inspector general puts Iran war cost at $33.4 billion, with up to 30 Reapers and dozens of other aircraft lost
beats.body: The first Lead Inspector General report on Operation Epic Fury tallies $33.4 billion in costs through June 29 -- $22.3 billion in expended munitions, $7.4 billion in obligations and $3.7 billion in equipment losses -- and counts as many as 30 MQ-9 Reapers along with F-15Es, an A-10 and helicopters destroyed; the report also lists 18 US troops killed and 417 wounded in the operation through that date.

beats.headline: Air Force secretary confirms for the first time that the US has weapons stationed in space
beats.body: Speaking at the Air, Space and Cyber Conference, Air Force Secretary Troy Meink said the US has fielded 'on-orbit space control weapons capable of defending the Joint Force against hostile adversary action' -- the first official US confirmation of space-based weapons, tied to the broader Golden Dome missile-defense buildup -- though he did not disclose what the weapons are or how they work.

beats.headline: Anthropic picks Nasdaq for a possible October IPO reportedly approaching a $2 trillion valuation
beats.body: Anthropic has selected Nasdaq over the NYSE for its planned public listing, with Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan leading an offering that could come as soon as October; the company has not yet filed publicly and must disclose financials at least 15 days before its investor roadshow begins, and the timing comes as AI-safety debate over frontier development continues to intensify.
